tagline: Two lanes through the San Gabriels, originally intended for fire access
intro: Angeles Crest Highway climbs from La Cañada Flintridge into the San Gabriel Mountains on two lanes, with switchbacks and blind curves in its eastern reaches. Much of the road passes through Angeles National Forest and the San Gabriel Mountains National Monument, where development is limited. The mountain corridor holds both National Forest Scenic Byway and California Scenic Highway designations. The approach from Foothill Boulevard follows a two-mile, 5 percent grade before entering the mountains.

Construction began in 1929 for a road originally intended to provide fire access. Prisoners from Camp 37 built it; World War II halted construction in 1941. Work resumed in 1946, and the completed highway opened in 1956. A proposed freeway upgrade in the 1950s was abandoned as geographically impractical.

The mountains continue to interrupt the road: the Mount Waterman account reports that a December 2025 landslide undermined the highway below the ski lift. Winter also normally closes the section from Islip Saddle to Vincent Gap because of rockfall and avalanche hazards.

From La Cañada Flintridge, the route reaches Red Box, where Mount Wilson Road branches away. Farther east come Islip Saddle and the highway’s high point at Dawson Saddle, followed by the descent through Big Pines toward Wrightwood.

moments.title: Red Box
moments.text: Red Box is a road junction on a 4,665-foot saddle between Mount Lawlor and San Gabriel Peak. The saddle divides the upper Arroyo Seco drainage from the West Fork of the San Gabriel River. Mount Wilson Road branches here, with the observatory about 4.5 miles from the highway. Its 100-inch Hooker telescope held the world’s largest aperture from 1917 to 1949. Edwin Hubble used it to establish that Andromeda was a galaxy beyond the Milky Way. Hubble and Milton Humason’s observations with the Hooker also supported Hubble’s 1929 paper showing that the universe is expanding.

moments.title: Islip Saddle
moments.text: At Islip Saddle, the Pacific Crest Trail crosses SR 2 at the head of San Gabriel Canyon. Mount Williamson stands to the northwest and Mount Islip to the southeast. The pass takes its name from George Islip, a Canadian homesteader who lived in neighboring San Gabriel Canyon in the 1900s. Two gates mark limits on road travel: one east of the parking lot restricts the winter route to Vincent Gap, while another south of the saddle blocks the northern portion of SR 39. On the highway, only nearby Dawson Saddle is a higher mountain pass.

moments.title: Big Pines
moments.text: Los Angeles County built Big Pines as a year-round recreation area in 1924. The community occupies Swarthout Valley, with Wrightwood and the San Bernardino County line on its eastern side. Until 1937, the ski area formed part of a Los Angeles County park. Its winter-sports history continued after World War II, when the 1946–47 season brought a new chairlift and the Sepp Benedikter Ski School. West of Big Pines lies Jackson Lake, a sag pond on the San Andreas Fault.

practical: Islip Saddle: The highway generally closes between Islip Saddle and Vincent Gap from mid-December to mid-May for snow and rockfall. Northern SR 39 is closed to automobile traffic. (checked 2026-10-11)
